 Starting XI presented by Modelo: LA Galaxy vs Austin FC | October 31, 2026
 LA Galaxy Communications
 Copy URL 
 Share on Facebook 
 Share on X 
 Starting XI:  GK JT Marcinkowski; D Harbor Miller, D Justin Haak, D Emiro Garcés, D John Nelson; M Pablo Ruiz, M Sergi Roberto, M Marco Reus; F Hirving Lozano, F Joseph Paintsil, F João Klauss
 Substitutes:  GK Novak Mićović, D Jakob Glesnes, D Julián Aude, D Lucas Calegari, M Elijah Wynder, M Lucas Sanabria, F Erik Thommy, F Robert Taylor, F Kyōgo Furuhashi
 *
Lineup Notes: *
 #1 Novak Mićović , 24, started the club’s first match post-World Cup break against LAFC. He earned his first clean sheet of the 2026 campaign in the club’s win over Charlotte FC back on February 28. In 2025, the Serbian goalkeeper completed his jump to the first team squad, earning 27 starts in all competitions after averaging four starts in first two seasons with the club. Notably, Mićović saved four of eight penalty kicks faced in shootouts throughout the 2023 campaign while playing in MLS NEXT Pro with LA Galaxy II.
 #2 Lucas Calegari , 24, rejoined the Galaxy in September after spending the past season with Eyüpspor, where he recorded a goal and four assists in 25 appearances across all competitions. The Cuiabá, Brazil native joined Eyüpspor on a permanent transfer in August 2025 after spending the previous 11 years under contract with Fluminense FC. Calegari initially joined the Brazilian club’s academy at the age of 12 and rose through the ranks to the first team, making his professional debut in 2020. In total, he recorded a goal and two assists in 86 appearances for his boyhood club, including 10 in the Copa Libertadores, and helped the side capture the Campeonato Carioca in 2022. In March 2023, Calegari embarked on a loan stint with the LA Galaxy as a U22 Initiative player. During that campaign, the defender started 27 consecutive matches for the Galaxy before seeing his season come to an abrupt end due to injury. Prior to the setback, Calegari earned MLS Team of the Matchday honors for registering two assists in a 3-2 road victory over Real Salt Lake and was ultimately voted as the club’s 2023 Defender of the Year at season’s end. Internationally, Calegari has represented Brazil at both the U-17 and U-20 levels.
 #3 Julián Aude , 23, has recorded 113 appearances for LA in all competitions since arriving at the club in 2023. Through 2025, Aude tallied a goal and two assists in 75 league games. The Argentine youth international defender finished the 2025 campaign with 1,888 minutes, his highest single-season minutes total with LA to date. Aude, who occupies an MLS U22 Initiative roster spot, is under contract through the end of the 2027 MLS season.
 #4 Maya Yoshida , 38, is out tonight with a leg injury. He was called up by the Japan National Team to play in the 2026 Kirin Challenge Cup in Tokyo to play in his final game for his country. He then traveled with the Japan National Team in a Special Assistant role throughout their 2026 World Cup campaign before returning to Los Angeles. For the Galaxy, Yoshida scored the opening goal of the match against Austin on April 11 in the 701st appearance of his professional career. The goal was his first of the 2026 campaign, his seventh for the Galaxy since 2023, and the 35th of his career. Yoshida completed 95.6% (391/409) of his passes in this season’s Concacaf Champions Cup, the highest of any player to attempt 250 or more passes in a single edition of the tournament since at least 2016-17. The Japanese international made over 450 professional appearances in the top leagues of England, Germany, Italy, Japan and Netherlands since making his professional debut in 2007. Yoshida has tallied 12 goals and three assists in 126 career appearances (120 starts) for the Japanese National Team. Yoshida has played in three FIFA World Cups (2014, 2018, 2022) and captained Japan to the Round of 16 of the 2022 edition of the FIFA World Cup. Notably, Yoshida was the only player on the Galaxy roster to appear in every MLS match (regular season and playoffs) during the 2024 season. 
 #5 Jakob Glesnes , 32, had his contract extended in March after joining LA in December. He spent the previous six seasons with the Philadelphia Union, where he became a two-time MLS Best XI member (2022, 2025), a three-time MLS All-Star (2022, 2023, 2025), and was named the 2022 MLS Defender of the Year. In the 2025 season, the center back totaled three goal contributions (1 goal, 2 assists) and 30 clearances in 31 matches played (30 starts) across MLS competition. The Norwegian recorded the second-most minutes (2,626) for the club in the 2025 season and led the Union defense to a best-in-league fewest goals conceded (35) and 14 clean sheets. Glesnes has played 182 games with 179 starts in his MLS career, recording nine goals and 10 assists. Before joining the Union, Glesnes played in Norway’s top division, the Eliteserien, representing Strømsgodset Toppfotball. 
 #6 Sergi Roberto , 34, registered his first assist as a member of the LA Galaxy at home against San Diego on October 17. Roberto has continued to lead MLS with a 95.4% pass success rate (per 90 minutes) since his arrival to LA. He made his home debut at Dignity Health Sports Park on September 5 in his first start for the Galaxy. He joined the G’s following two seasons with Como 1907 in Italy’s Serie A that succeeded a decorated 18-year career with FC Barcelona in Spain. His time with Barcelona produced 25 trophies including seven La Liga championships, six Copa del Rey titles, six Spanish Super Cups, two UEFA Champions League trophies, two FIFA Club World Cups, and two UEFA Super Cups. Roberto wore the captain’s armband for Barça during the 2023–24 season. The former Spanish National Team midfielder earned more than 400 appearances for club and country during his stint in Barcelona. Notably, the signing reunites Roberto with current LA Galaxy midfielder Riqui Puig, his former teammate at FC Barcelona from 2018-2022.  
 #7 Kyōgo Furuhashi , 31, is back on the bench for the Galaxy today after missing the previous three matches due to an injury he suffered in St. Louis on October 11. He had started in nine of his 11 appearances since his arrival to the club in July. He joined LA via a transfer from Birmingham City, where he recorded three goals in 31 appearances across all competitions during the 2025-26 campaign. Prior to his move to England, the Japanese forward made six appearances for French Ligue 1 side Stade Rennais after joining near the end of 2025. Prior to that, Furuhashi tallied 85 goals and 19 assists in 165 appearances across all competitions for Celtic, helping the Scottish club capture eight domestic trophies, including four Scottish Premiership titles. During the 2022-23 campaign, Furuhashi recorded 34 goals across all competitions, earned Scottish Premiership Player of the Year and Golden Boot honors and helped Celtic complete a domestic treble. Before moving to Europe, Furuhashi began his professional career with FC Gifu in Japan’s J2 League before joining Vissel Kobe in 2018, where he helped the club win the Emperor’s Cup and Japanese Super Cup in 2020. Notably, Furuhashi scored 15 goals in 21 league appearances for Kobe during the 2021 campaign to earn his move to Celtic. At the international level, Furuhashi has made 23 appearances for the Japan National Team since making his senior debut in 2019.
 #8 Lucas Sanabria , 22, added his first MLS assist in the club’s draw with Vancouver on May 2. He scored his second goal of the campaign in Dallas on April 18. He opened his 2026 goal scoring account in the club’s victory at home over Charlotte FC on February 28. He opened the scoring and set the tone for the club’s three-goal night. Sanabria tallied two goals and an assist in 26 appearances during his first season with LA in 2025. At the international level, Sanabria was called in by the Uruguayan National Team for 2026 FIFA World Cup Qualifying for matches against Peru on Oct. 11 and Ecuador on Oct. 15. Prior to joining the Galaxy, Sanabria recorded five goals and four assists in 46 matches played (41 starts) across all competitions for Club Nacional in Uruguay. The Florida, Uruguay, native tallied one goal in 11 appearances (all starts) for Nacional during the 2023-24 Copa Libertadores, helping his club reach the Round of 16. He later scored two goals in four matches to help Nacional reach the 2024 Copa AUF Uruguay Final. Sanabria was also a part of the Nacional side that won the 2024 edition of the Torneo Intermedio, logging one goal and two assists in seven appearances (all starts) throughout the competition.
 #11 Hirving Lozano , 31, makes his official return to the Galaxy lineup this afternoon after recovering from an injury he suffered while on international duty with the Mexican national team. He recorded his first assist for the Galaxy against New England on September 5, one week after scoring his first goal in Galaxy blue, white, and gold against his former squad in San Diego on August 29. He made his LA Galaxy debut in Houston on August 15 and his first club start four days later against San Jose in his Dignity Health Sports Park debut. On August 7, he joined the Galaxy via loan from San Diego FC, where he recorded nine goals and 10 assists in 27 appearances as the club’s first-ever Designated Player. Prior to his time in San Diego, Lozano returned to PSV Eindhoven for a stint from 2023-24 after previously playing for the club from 2017-2018. He scored 51 goals and added 28 assists for PSV overall, enroute to helping the club claim Eredivisie titles in 2017-18, 2023-24, and 2024-25. Before his move to PSV, Lozano played for Italian Serie A side Napoli, where he registered 30 goals and 17 assists in 155 appearances and played a key role in delivering the club's first Scudetto in more than three decades during the 2022–23 campaign. He began his career via the Pachuca academy, where he rose to the first team and recorded 43 goals and 31 assists in 149 appearances across all competitions. He helped the club capture the Liga MX Clausura title in 2016 as well as the 2016–17 Concacaf Champions League, in which he earned the Golden Boot with his competition leading 8 goals. Internationally, Lozano has earned 75 caps and contributed 18 goals and 12 assists for Mexico. At the 2018 FIFA World Cup, his goal against Germany secured a historic victory over the defending world champions. Across his international career, Lozano has represented Mexico in some of the sport’s biggest competitions, including the 2016 Copa América, the 2017 FIFA Confederations Cup, the Concacaf Nations League, the 2021 Concacaf Gold Cup, and the 2018 and 2022 FIFA World Cups.
 #12 JT Marcinkowski , 29, put pen to paper on a new contract extension with the Galaxy in September, keeping him in LA through the 2028-29 season. He delivered an MLS Team of the Matchday performance against San Jose on Matchday 18, including a crucial late-match penalty kick save that preserved a result for the Galaxy against his former club in San Jose. Marcinkowski recorded a six-save clean sheet at Lumen Field in Seattle in mid-May amidst. He recorded a Galaxy career-high nine saves in the club’s victory over Real Salt Lake on April 26, one off his career high mark of 10 set in 2021 with San Jose. Marcinkowski has recorded three clean sheets so far in 2026 CCC play. The first shutout came in a Round One second leg match against Sporting San Miguelito on February 25, while the second came in the first leg of the club’s fixture against Mount Pleasant FA back on March 11. The third and most recent shutout occurred at National Stadium in Jamaica a week later. He joined the LA Galaxy ahead of the 2025 campaign and recorded one clean sheet in three spot starts for the club in league play. The Alamo, California native signed a Homegrown contract with the San Jose Earthquakes in 2017 after developing in the club’s academy. The 2021 MLS Regular Season saw Marcinkowski post a career-high five shutouts and 129 saves in 33 matches played (all starts) for the Earthquakes. In total, Marcinkowski logged 19 shutouts and 330 saves in 96 appearances (95 starts) in five seasons with San Jose.
 #14 John Nelson  earned his 100th LA Galaxy appearance in all competitions on September 19 against Minnesota. He had his contract extended following a strong 2025 campaign that saw him named LA Galaxy’s Defender of the Year. The 27-year-old appeared in a career-high 31 matches with 24 starts and added a career-best three assists. Defensively, Nelson recorded 36 aerial duels won and 22 clearances while playing a key role in two of the Galaxy’s four shutout wins across all competitions. A steady presence on the back line since joining the LA Galaxy ahead of the 2024 season, Nelson recorded his first career MLS goal (Regular Season or Playoffs) and an assist in LA’s 5-0 win over the Colorado Rapids at Dignity Health Sports Park in the Round One Best-of-3 Series opener of the 2025 MLS Cup Playoffs on Oct. 26, 2024. In his two previous seasons with LA, Nelson made more than 70 appearances, contributing one goal and three assists. Drafted 10th overall by FC Dallas in the 2019 MLS SuperDraft after a standout collegiate career at the University of North Carolina, the Medina, Ohio native spent two seasons with Dallas before joining FC Cincinnati ahead of the 2022 campaign.
 #15 Justin Haak , 24, registered his second goal of the season for the Galaxy in the win over Portland on October 14. He scored the game-winning goal for LA against Colorado on September 26, his first goal as a member of the Galaxy. Previously, he assisted the Galaxy’s lone goal on May 13 in Kansas City. He added his first assist for LA against Dallas on April 18. He joined the LA Galaxy after seven seasons with New York City FC for which he appeared in 111 matches (75 starts) in all competitions. In 2025, Haak appeared in all 34 matches (all starts) for NYCFC and came just 50 minutes shy of an Iron Man season in MLS play. In addition, the Brooklyn, New York native recorded one goal and four assists while also scoring his first career playoff goal in the club's loss to Miami. Haak’s professional career began with NYCFC in 2019 when he signed a Homegrown contract following four years of development within the club’s academy system.
 #17 Pablo Ruiz , 27, registered his first assist as a member of the Blue, White, and Gold against Portland earlier this month. He became just the third player in LA Galaxy history to score his first career goal for the club via a direct free kick on September 19, joining Ned Grabavoy (7/10/04) and Douglas Costa (3/12/22). He made his first start for the Galaxy in Vancouver on September 9, shortly after his deadline trade to Los Angeles earlier in the month. He made his club debut at home last weekend against New England as a second-half substitute. He joined the LA Galaxy following eight and a half seasons with Western Conference side Real Salt Lake, where he registered nine goals and 19 assists in 162 appearances (124 starts) across all competitions. Notably, Ruiz scored two goals in 2026 Leagues Cup play, one against Tigres UANL on August 4, and another against Atalante on August 8. Prior to the start of his professional career in Salt Lake, Ruiz developed in the academies of C.A.I. and San Lorenzo in Argentina. He then moved to Chile, where he played for San Luis in the Chilean Primera División. After that, Ruiz traveled stateside to sign with Real Salt Lake in February 2018. Internationally, the left-footed midfielder has represented Argentina at the U-17 level, where he scored two goals in 10 appearances across both the 2015 South American U-17 Championship and the FIFA U-17 World Cup.
 #18 Marco Reus , 36, returns to the lineup today after missing the previous contest due to illness and will look to pick up right where he left off. He has been in flying form with nine goal contributions (four goals, five assists) in his last eight matches. He recorded his fifth dual-contribution match of the campaign on October 14 against Portland, adding both a goal and an assist in the club’s home victory. He recorded the game equalizing assist four minutes before scoring the game-winning goal in Minnesota and earned three MLS Team of the Matchday honors in September. He recorded an assist in the club’s win over San Jose on August 19 and has now added an assist in each of the club’s outings against the Earthquakes this season. He recorded the game-winning assist in Seattle on May 16 and added an assist off the bench in the club’s victory over Atlanta the weekend before. He recorded a game-winning brace against Real Salt Lake on April 26, a performance that featured a picture-perfect free kick from just above the box to open the scoring on the night. Earlier this year, Reus signed a contract extension with the Galaxy that keeps the decorated midfielder in LA through December 2027. He recorded an assist in his 2026 debut in the club’s home opener against NYCFC and took just 85 seconds to do so. Through 2025, Reus has appeared in 43 matches (32 starts) across all competitions for the Galaxy since his arrival in LA and has recorded nine goals and 14 assists overall. He had an assist in four matches played (two starts) during the Audi 2024 MLS Cup Playoffs. Reus signed with the Galaxy on August 15, 2024, following a decorated, 12-year career at Borussia Dortmund, where he totaled 301 goal contributions (170 goals, 131 assists) in 429 appearances across all competitions. Notably, Reus was twice named the German Footballer of the Year (2012, 2019), was recognized as a three-time Bundesliga Player of the Year (2011-12, 2013-14, 2018-19), was named to the UEFA Team of the Year (2013) and helped Dortmund win the German Cup (2016-17, 2020-21), the DFB-Pokal (2016-17, 2020-21) and the DFL-Supercup (2013, 2019) two times each. At the international level, Reus has tallied 15 goals and 14 assists in 48 career appearances (34 starts) for the German National Team (2011-21).
 #21 Robert Taylor,  31, recorded an assist in the club’s draw with LAFC, his fifth goal contribution (one goal, four assists) in his last six matches. He registered an assist against Portland on October 14 to cap off a streak of four consecutive matches with a goal contribution. He opened his Galaxy goalscoring account against New England on September 5. He made his club debut on July 17 against LAFC at Dignity Health Sports Park. He previously spent parts of the 2025 and 2026 seasons with Austin FC, where he recorded one goal and one assist in 24 appearances across all competitions. He joined Austin midway through the 2025 campaign following a trade from Inter Miami. During his three-plus seasons with Miami from 2022-25, Taylor made 116 appearances across all competitions, tallying 18 goals and 18 assists while helping the club win the 2023 Leagues Cup and the 2024 MLS Supporters’ Shield. Across his MLS career, Taylor has made 110 regular-season appearances, recording 14 goals and 12 assists. Before moving to MLS, Taylor had successful spells in Finland, Sweden, and Norway. His most productive stretch came with Norwegian side SK Brann, where he registered 14 goals and 16 assists in 60 appearances during the 2020 and 2021 seasons.  Taylor is under contract through the end of the 2026 MLS season with a club option for 2027. Internationally, Taylor has earned 34 caps for Finland, recording two goals and three assists. He represented his country at UEFA EURO 2020 and has been a regular contributor for the Finnish National Team throughout his career.  
 #22 Elijah Wynder , 23, returned to squad on September 26 following an ankle injury he suffered in Houston in mid-August. He tallied two goals and one assist in 18 league appearances (11 starts) in his first season with LA after his acquisition ahead of the 2025 campaign. The Oldham County, Kentucky native recorded 11 goals and three assists in 84 appearances (55 starts) across all competitions in his five seasons with Louisville City FC in USL Championship. In 2024, Wynder recorded six goals and two assists in 33 matches played (32 starts) enroute to being named the 2024 USL Championship Young Player of the Year, earning USL Championship All-League Second Team honors and helping Louisville City capture the club's first-ever USL Championship Players' Shield. Two years prior, after returning from a loan stint with FC Tucson, Wynder recorded two goals in 13 appearances across all competitions on his way to receiving the 2022 USL Championship Comeback Player of the Year award. Notably, Wynder's scored the game-winning goal in the Eastern Conference Final of the 2022 USL Championship Playoffs to earn the club's fourth Eastern Conference title in club history. 
 #25 Emiro Garcés , 24, earns his fourth consecutive start today, and 13th of the season so far. He recorded the game-winning assist in Austin on April 11 and added another assist that week in Columbus. He has seen regular minutes over the past 10 matches (eight starts) since returning from an early season injury. Last season, he saw his first career MLS and Galaxy goal come in a 2-2 draw against Minnesota United FC on March 22, 2025. Two weeks later, the 24-year-old Columbian scored again, this time in the Concacaf Champions Cup Quarterfinal second leg against Tigres on April 8. In total, Garcés has recorded the two aforementioned goals and three assists in 50 appearances (35 starts) across all competitions over the past two seasons. The defender previously made 67 appearances (57 starts) across all competitions for Deportivo Pereira (2021-24), helping the club win its first-ever league title during the 2022 Liga BetPlay Dimayor I campaign. At the international level, Garcés was previously called up by the Colombian National Team for a domestic training camp back in October 2022.
 #26 Harbor Miller , 19, registered an assist against San Diego on October 17 and was named to his first MLS Team of the Matchday as a result. He earns his 20th league start of the season tonight. He joined the U.S. U-20 Men’s National Team for the recent September-October window in which he started and played 90 minutes at right back for the Stars-and-Stripes in a friendly against Brazil. He recorded the game-winning assist on August 19 against San Jose. Coming out of the league’s World Cup break, Miller started in nine consecutive matches at right back, a position that Head Coach Greg Vanney has often referred to as his long-term spot. He recorded the game-winning assist in the club’s 3-0 rout of Mount Pleasant FA in the CCC Round of 16 in March. His first start of the 2026 MLS Regular Season came on March 14 against Sporting Kansas City, while his first appearance of the year came against Charlotte FC on Feb 28. In 2025, he tallied one goal and two assists in 10 appearances (nine starts) across all competitions in his first season with the LA Galaxy. Miller recorded nine goal contributions (five goals, four assists) in 16 appearances (all starts) on loan with Ventura County FC during the 2025 MLS NEXT Pro Regular Season. Notably, the Fullerton, California native is the seventh-youngest player in team history (17 years, 8 months, 11 days) to make their LA Galaxy and MLS debut. Miller tallied one goal and two assists in 22 matches played (18 starts) across all competitions for Ventura County FC during the 2024 campaign. Miller was named the MLS NEXT Cup MVP presented by adidas after the LA Galaxy Academy U-17s defeated Real Colorado 4-2 in the final of the 2023 U-17 MLS NEXT Cup on June 25, 2023. Miller was named to the second-annual MLS NEXT All-Star Game presented by Allstate during the 2023 campaign. Miller signed a three-year contract as a Homegrown Player with the Galaxy beginning in 2025 through the end of the 2027 MLS season with a club option for 2028.
 #27 Erik Thommy , 32, scored his second goal of the season against San Diego FC on October 17, his first at Dignity Health Sports Park. He recorded two assists in the club’s match in St. Louis. He came off the bench in his return to Sporting Park to face his former club Sporting KC on May 13 and recorded his first assist as a member of the Galaxy. He opened his LA Galaxy account with the game-winning goal in Austin on April 11. He joined the Galaxy following a three-and-a-half-year stint with Sporting Kansas City. In total, Thommy has paired 19 goals with 10 assists in nearly 7,100 minutes across 101 MLS matches (82 starts). Prior to his time in the States, Thommy played professionally for nine seasons in his native Germany, accumulating a total of 42 goals and 33 assists.
 #28 Joseph Paintsil , 28, came out firing against LAFC last weekend, recording a brace in the team’s 2-2 draw away from home, and received his first MLS Team of the Matchday honor of the season for his performance. He has now recorded seven goals and five assists in league play this season. He earned his first league start since returning from injury against Portland on October 14. He initially returned to the pitch and the scoresheet in the club’s friendly against Cruz Azul on October 4. He previously found the scoresheet in the club’s first meeting with San Jose this season and did so against them again on August 19 to secure all three points for the G’s at home. He scored the Galaxy’s lone goal against the Houston Dynamo and added an assist on the club’s game-winning goal in Atlanta on May 9, within weeks of scoring the club’s lone goal against Vancouver. He has missed eight league matches due to injury this season. Paintsil finished the 2025 campaign with 15 goals and six assists across 34 matches played (31 starts) in all competitions for the LA Galaxy. Last season, Paintsil became just the third Galaxy player all-time to score a first-half hat trick in an MLS match in the team’s 4-1 win over Sporting Kansas City on September 27. The performance earned Paintsil the MLS Player of the Matchday for Matchdays 36 and 37. He has recorded 48 goal contributions (30 goals, 18 assists) in 72 career matches played (68 starts) across all competitions for LA. Paintsil was acquired by the Galaxy from Belgian Pro League side K.R.C. Genk as a Designated Player and was signed to a four-year contract through the end of the 2027 MLS season. During the 2022-23 Belgian Pro League season, Paintsil notched 28 goal contributions (14 goals, 14 assists) in 30 league appearances (28 starts), helping Genk qualify for the 2023-24 Europa Conference League. At the international level, Paintsil has notched two assists in 15 appearances (9 starts) for Ghana. The team qualified for the 2026 FIFA World Cup by defeating Central African Republic and Comoros in October 2025.
 #99 João Klauss  has registered nine goals in just 15 league appearances this season, with his latest coming in the Galaxy’s previous home contest against San Diego on October 17. He scored his eighth goal in his return to St. Louis on October 11. He scored the equalizing goal in both come-from-behind victories for LA against Minnesota and Colorado in September. He made his long-awaited return to the pitch for the Galaxy on September 12 after being sidelined since mid-April with a foot injury that ultimately required surgery. Prior to the injury, Klauss recorded eight goal contributions in 11 matches played across all competitions (six goals, two assists) and recorded five goals in seven matches in MLS competition. He was voted by Galaxy fans as the club’s Player of the Month in back-to-back months to start the 2026 campaign. Klauss arrived in LA this offseason following three seasons with St. Louis CITY SC, where he recorded 27 goals in 85 appearances for the 2023 expansion side. The 29-year-old Brazilian forward has extensive international experience, having competed in the German Bundesliga with Hoffenheim, the Austrian Bundesliga with LASK and the Belgian Pro League with Standard Liège. Throughout his time in Europe and in MLS, he has appeared in both the UEFA Europa League and the Concacaf Champions Cup, adding valuable global competition experience to his resume. In his MLS debut season with St. Louis in 2023, Klauss tallied 10 goals and two assists across 19 league matches. He repeated the feat in 2025, once again reaching double-digit goals with a 10-goal, two-assist campaign. On June 14, 2025, Klauss recorded a hat trick against the Galaxy, with the match ending in a 3-3 draw at Energizer Park. Klauss began his career in Brazil with Grêmio’s U-20 side. He joined St. Louis CITY SC in July 2022 as the club’s first-ever Designated Player.\
